item.title: Advise a Panel on Comparing Small Grant Projects
item.prompt_text: A public grants panel wants one measure for every funded project. A neighbourhood orchestra could count concert visitors, while a workshop that helps a few people finish a long project could track how often they return. The panel wants fair comparison and a way to explain awards publicly. Write a briefing that keeps one useful common standard, gives two different indicators, and explains how to handle a superficially impressive figure.
item.audience: a panel awarding grants to community projects
item.target_grammar: Nominalisation, qualification and parallel cases. Give an explicit condition for revising a judgement.
item.target_structure: Define the shared judgement, pair each activity with evidence of its purpose, and test one misleading success figure.

checklist.point: Give separate indicators for the two projects.
Explain why an impressive number may not show the intended result.
Show how the panel could report a clear and fair comparison.
